newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PENPIX OF MEN'S FINALISTS AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PENPIX OF MEN'S FINALISTS AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Portraits of Pete Sampras and Carlos Moya, who will meet in the final of the Australian Open on Sunday:

After a patchy start, world number one Sampras was on top form against Thomas Muster in the semifinals, taking just under two hours to beat him in straight sets. Only one of his eight Grand Slam wins to date has been achieved on the Melbourne hardcourt, in 1994. Is one of the finest servers and volleyers in the game and has flat, orthodox groundstrokes hit on the rise with awesome power. Holds a big advantage over his opponent in terms of experience.
Seeding: 1. Age: 25. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 77kg. Height: 1.85m. Ranking: 1. Tournament wins: 44. Career prize money: $25.5 million. Head-to-head: none.

The most talked-about player of the tournament, both on and off the court. He disposed of defending champion Boris Becker in the first round and has been growing in confidence ever since, culminating with a straight-sets victory over second seed Michael Chang in the semifinals. With his rock-star looks and relaxed attitude he has become a fans' favourite. A clay court specialist who favours his forehand, he is having a field day on the slow hardcourt surface. His never-say-die attitude and stamina could be a telling factor with temperatures forecast to soar in Melbourne. Lack of experience could be his downfall.
Seeding: None. Age: 20. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 80kg. Height: 1.90m. Ranking: 25. Tournament wins: 2. Career prize money: $590,000.
